written:
## 1. The numbers
Risk-off. A hotter-than-expected inflation report cemented bets that the Fed will raise rates next month, so tech, gold and crypto led the declines while the dollar and yields firmed.

## 2. What moved and why
**Hot inflation puts a December Fed hike on the table**
Why it happened: October CPI rose 0.4% against a consensus of 0.3%. Shorter-term Treasury yields jumped after the release.
Why it matters: A hike would raise borrowing costs for companies and deals, and it hits long-duration growth stocks hardest.

**Gold drops as yields and the dollar rise**
Why it happened: Stronger inflation data pushed Treasury yields and the dollar higher, and gold gave up recent gains. Profit-taking after Monday's rally added to the drop.
Why it matters: Higher yields and a firmer dollar raise the opportunity cost of holding non-yielding bullion.

**Bitcoin hits a near three-month low**
Why it happened: Risk-off trading hit crypto, and bitcoin hit its weakest level since Aug. 20. US spot bitcoin ETFs have also seen sustained selling pressure.
Why it matters: Crypto is trading like a leveraged bet on easy money, so rate-hike fears hit it harder than stocks.

## Deals
- **IPO: Anthropic → public markets: Anthropic** (Size of the raise not found). Reports point to a very large valuation, which would make it one of the biggest tech listings ever.
- **IPO: Barrick → NYSE listing of its North American unit: Barrick** (Size not disclosed). The unit will list in New York, which is a negative signal for Toronto's capital markets.

## Already out today
- Before 8:30 AM: Fed Governor Waller's remarks. He called for higher rates vs No consensus expected. It reinforces a December hike.
- 8:30 AM: US October CPI. 0.4% m/m vs 0.3% m/m expected. A hotter print keeps the Fed on a tightening path.
- 8:30 AM: US October core CPI. 0.3% m/m vs 0.2% m/m expected. Underlying inflation is not cooling.

## 3. What's coming today
- 12:00 PM: EIA Short-Term Energy Outlook. It sets the official view on oil supply and prices.
- 1:00 PM: 10-year Treasury note auction. Demand will show appetite for duration after the CPI move.
- 1:30 PM: Fed's Schmid speaks. Another read on the December decision.
- 3:30 PM: Fed Governor Bowman speaks. A voter commenting on inflation.
- 4:30 PM: API crude inventories. An early read on US oil stocks.
- Evening: Philadelphia Fed's Paulson speaks. A voter on the outlook.

## 4. Canada corner
- TSX: No live reading this morning. The index surged to a two-month high on Monday. TSX futures were little changed before the bell.
- Loonie: USD/CAD pushed toward 1.42 as an 18% oil slump and a 148 bp yield gap left the loonie exposed. WTI is down roughly 18% this month on Middle East de-escalation hopes.
- Bank of Canada: The October hike now faces lower energy prices, and the Summary of Deliberations is on today's calendar. Before today's CPI, markets priced about a 40% chance of a BoC hike in December versus roughly 84% for the Fed.
- Jobs: Canadian employment fell for a third straight month in October and the unemployment rate rose to 6.7%.

## 5. The takeaway
IB & Markets: If someone asks you about markets today: a hotter CPI print pushed December Fed-hike odds higher, lifting short-term yields and the dollar. Tech, gold and crypto fell together, while small caps and defensives held up better.
Consulting angle: Higher-for-longer rates raise the cost of capital for AI-heavy and leveraged businesses. A sensible strategy is to stress-test capex plans and financing at higher hurdle rates, and to avoid funding growth that only works at low rates.
Accounting angle: For a large IPO such as Anthropic's, direct issuance costs are deducted from equity proceeds rather than expensed. Auditors would focus on revenue recognition, share-based compensation and valuation of any pre-IPO instruments. For Barrick's US listing, expect questions on carve-out financials and segment reporting.

stories.why_happened: October CPI rose 0.4% against a consensus of 0.3%. Shorter-term Treasury yields jumped after the release.
stories.why_matters: A hike would raise borrowing costs for companies and deals, and it hits long-duration growth stocks hardest.
stories.full: Monday was the S&P 500's best day in seven months, coming two sessions after its worst day in 18 months. Part of the swing came from a rotation out of AI plays into defensive sectors like healthcare. The Fed raised rates in September and paused in October. Today's report undercut the relief. Core prices rose 0.3% in October, hotter than expected, and have risen 0.3% or more in 5 of 2026's first 10 months. Futures now fully price a 25 bp Fed hike in December. Fed Governor Waller suggested even a 50 bp move could be appropriate. The split was visible at the open. The Nasdaq dropped while the small-cap Russell 2000 gained. That fits money moving away from crowded AI trades. Leveraged funds and momentum traders were already hurting. Nvidia fell 4.3% on Monday after reports about CEO Jensen Huang's alleged links to a woman suspected of Chinese intelligence ties. Watch the Fed speakers and Friday's PPI. The next Fed meeting is December 9.

stories.title: Gold drops as yields and the dollar rise
stories.why_happened: Stronger inflation data pushed Treasury yields and the dollar higher, and gold gave up recent gains. Profit-taking after Monday's rally added to the drop.
stories.why_matters: Higher yields and a firmer dollar raise the opportunity cost of holding non-yielding bullion.
stories.full: Gold had just reached a three-week high. A weaker dollar had also supported bullion. That support faded once the CPI print revived the dollar's rate advantage. Gold was already softening before the data. Hawkish Fed comments weighed on it ahead of CPI. Silver fell more than 3% to $51.72 as both headline and core CPI beat forecasts. Gold miners and bullion ETF holders lose when real yields rise. Importers priced in other currencies also pay more as the dollar firms. The path from here depends on how aggressive the Fed sounds. A 50 bp hike in December would add pressure, while softer data would let gold recover.

stories.title: Bitcoin hits a near three-month low
stories.why_happened: Risk-off trading hit crypto, and bitcoin hit its weakest level since Aug. 20. US spot bitcoin ETFs have also seen sustained selling pressure.
stories.why_matters: Crypto is trading like a leveraged bet on easy money, so rate-hike fears hit it harder than stocks.
stories.full: Bitcoin fell below $75,000 after recording its lowest weekly close since August. Spot bitcoin ETFs saw $1.28 billion in weekly outflows, and $1.04 billion of leveraged longs were liquidated. About $200 million more in leveraged positions reportedly unwound within five minutes of the CPI release. Smaller coins fell further. Ether, XRP and solana were down closer to 6%. Corporate holders are under pressure too. Strategy, the largest listed corporate holder, is now below its average purchase price. Watch ETF flows and whether another leveraged-long liquidation wave follows. Stock moves after the Fed speakers will also matter, because crypto has been tracking risk appetite.

I could not confirm a filing date, proceeds or exchange from the sources I could access. The valuation range, if accurate, would put the company among the largest listed tech names on day one. The AI sell-off and the Fed outlook will shape whether the market has appetite for a deal this size. Watch for a public filing, which would disclose revenue and losses, share structure and the planned raise.

deals.type: IPO: Barrick → NYSE listing of its North American unit
deals.why: The unit will list in New York, which is a negative signal for Toronto's capital markets.
deals.full: In a filing alongside its third-quarter earnings, Barrick said it expects its North American unit to be listed on the NYSE. I did not find terms, a timeline or the share of the unit to be sold. Gold-sector bankers and Canadian exchange officials will watch for the structure, since a US primary listing moves fee pools and trading volume south.

intern.headline: Hot inflation report revives bets on a Fed rate hike, stocks slide
intern.mood: Risk-off. Investors are nervous. A higher-than-expected inflation report made it more likely that the Fed (the US central bank) will raise interest rates next month. Tech stocks, gold and crypto fell the most, while the dollar and bond yields (the interest rate a government or company pays to borrow money) went up.

stories.title: Hot inflation puts a December Fed rate hike on the table
stories.why_happened: October CPI (the Consumer Price Index, a common measure of inflation) rose 0.4%. Economists had expected 0.3%. Short-term Treasury yields (the interest rates on short-term US government loans) jumped right after the report.
stories.why_matters: A rate hike makes borrowing more expensive for companies and for deals. Fast-growing tech stocks, whose value depends on profits far in the future, usually take the biggest hit.
stories.full: Monday was the S&P 500's best day in seven months. That came just two trading days after its worst day in 18 months. Part of the swing came from investors moving money out of AI stocks and into defensive sectors (steady industries like healthcare that people need in good times and bad). Today's report took back some of that relief. Core prices (inflation without food and energy, which can jump around a lot) rose 0.3% in October. That was hotter than expected. Core prices have risen 0.3% or more in 5 of the first 10 months of 2026. Futures (bets on where prices will go) now fully price in a 25 basis point hike (a quarter of a percentage point) by the Fed in December. Fed Governor Waller said even a 50 basis point move could be right. The split was clear when the market opened. The Nasdaq (a tech-heavy stock index) fell, while the Russell 2000 (a index of smaller US companies) rose. That fits money leaving crowded AI trades. Leveraged funds (investment funds that borrow money to bet bigger) and momentum traders (people who buy stocks that are already rising) were already losing money. Nvidia fell 4.3% on Monday after reports about CEO Jensen Huang's alleged links to a woman suspected of Chinese intelligence ties. Watch what Fed speakers say, and Friday's PPI (producer prices, a measure of inflation at the wholesale level). The next Fed meeting is on December 9.

stories.title: Gold drops as bond yields and the dollar rise
stories.why_happened: Stronger inflation data pushed Treasury yields and the dollar higher. Gold gave up recent gains. Some investors also sold to take profits after Monday's rally.
stories.why_matters: When yields and the dollar rise, holding gold becomes less attractive. Gold pays no interest, so the interest you could earn elsewhere becomes a bigger cost (this is called opportunity cost).
stories.full: Gold had just hit a three-week high. A weaker dollar had helped support it. That help faded once the CPI report made the dollar stronger, since higher US interest rates make the dollar more attractive. Gold was already getting weaker before the data came out. Hawkish comments from the Fed (comments that suggest higher rates) pushed it down ahead of CPI. Silver fell more than 3% to $51.72 after both headline and core CPI came in above forecasts. Gold miners (companies that dig gold out of the ground) and people who own gold through ETFs (exchange-traded funds, which are funds you can buy like a stock) lose out when real yields (interest rates after inflation) rise. Businesses that buy goods priced in other currencies also pay more when the dollar gets stronger. What happens next depends on how strongly the Fed sounds. A 50 basis point hike in December would add more pressure. Softer data would let gold recover.

stories.title: Bitcoin hits a near three-month low
stories.why_happened: Investors moved away from risky assets, and crypto was hit hard. Bitcoin fell to its weakest level since August 20. Investors have also been steadily selling US spot bitcoin ETFs (funds that hold actual bitcoin and trade like stocks).
stories.why_matters: Crypto often moves like a bet on cheap money. When rate hikes look likely, it can fall harder than stocks.
stories.full: Bitcoin fell below $75,000. It had just posted its lowest weekly close since August. Investors pulled $1.28 billion out of spot bitcoin ETFs in one week. Also, $1.04 billion of leveraged longs (bets that prices will rise, made with borrowed money) were forced to close. Reports say about $200 million more in leveraged bets closed within five minutes of the CPI release. Smaller coins fell further. Ether, XRP and Solana were each down closer to 6%. Companies that hold bitcoin are under pressure too. Strategy, the largest listed company holding bitcoin, is now trading below the average price it paid for its bitcoin. Watch the ETF money flows (whether money is going in or out) and whether another wave of forced selling of leveraged bets happens. Stock moves after the Fed speakers will matter too, since crypto has been moving with how willing investors are to take risks.

deals.type: IPO (Initial Public Offering, when a private company first sells shares to the public)
deals.value: Size of the raise not found. Reports point to a very large valuation (the estimated total value of the company), which would make it one of the biggest tech listings ever.
deals.why: If it happens, it would be one of the largest tech stock sales ever. Its success depends on whether investors want to buy stock after the AI sell-off.
deals.full: A headline on November 10 said an Anthropic IPO would value the maker of Claude between about $917 billion and $1.02 trillion. I could not confirm a filing date, the amount of money raised or the stock exchange from the sources I could access. If the valuation range is accurate, the company would be among the largest listed tech companies on its first day of trading. The AI sell-off and the Fed's plans will shape whether investors want to buy a deal this big. Watch for a public filing. That filing would show revenue and losses, how the shares are split up, and how much money the company plans to raise.

deals.type: IPO (Initial Public Offering) of its North American unit, listing on the NYSE (New York Stock Exchange)
deals.why: The unit will be listed in New York. The Globe and Mail said this is a setback for Canada's stock markets, because it may take trading and fees away from Toronto.
deals.full: In a filing released with its third-quarter earnings (the profit report for July to September), Barrick said it expects its North American unit to be listed on the NYSE. The Globe and Mail described this as a setback for Canadian capital markets. The likely reasons are easier access to deeper US investor demand and a possibly higher valuation. I did not find the terms, a timeline or how much of the unit will be sold. Gold-sector bankers and Canadian exchange officials will watch the deal structure closely, since a main US listing moves fees and trading volume to the US.

Prices rose faster than expected, so the Fed may keep raising rates.

Loonie (Canadian dollar): USD/CAD (how many Canadian dollars one US dollar buys) moved toward 1.42. Oil fell 18% and there is a 148 basis point gap between Canadian and US interest rates, which leaves the loonie under pressure. WTI (a main oil price benchmark) is down about 18% this month on hopes that tensions in the Middle East are easing.

Bank of Canada (Canada's central bank): The October rate hike now faces lower energy prices. The Summary of Deliberations (the central bank's meeting notes) is on today's calendar. Before today's CPI, markets priced about a 40% chance of a Bank of Canada hike in December, versus about 84% for the Fed.
Jobs: Canadian employment fell for a third straight month in October. The unemployment rate rose to 6.7%.
intern.takeaway: IB & Markets: If someone asks you about markets today, here is the short version. A hotter inflation report made investors expect a Fed rate hike in December. That pushed bond yields and the dollar up. Tech stocks, gold and crypto fell together, while small companies and steady defensive sectors held up better.
intern.takeaway_consulting: Higher-for-longer rates (rates that stay high for a long time) make it more expensive for companies to fund growth. This hits AI-heavy and heavily borrowed businesses hardest. A sensible plan is to test spending and borrowing plans at higher interest rates. Avoid growth plans that only work when money is cheap.
intern.takeaway_accounting: For a large IPO like Anthropic's, the direct costs of issuing shares are taken off the money raised, instead of being counted as an expense. Auditors would focus on how revenue is recorded, stock-based pay for employees, and how any shares issued before the IPO are valued. For Barrick's US listing, expect questions about carve-out financials (separate financial statements for one part of a company) and segment reporting (breaking results into business areas).

I did not find terms, a timeline or the share of the unit to be sold. Gold-sector bankers and Canadian exchange officials will watch for the structure, since a US primary listing moves fee pools and trading volume south.

canada: TSX: No live reading this morning. The index surged to a two-month high on Monday. TSX futures were little changed before the bell.
Loonie: USD/CAD pushed toward 1.42 as an 18% oil slump and a 148 bp yield gap left the loonie exposed. WTI is down roughly 18% this month on Middle East de-escalation hopes.

Bank of Canada: The October hike now faces lower energy prices, and the Summary of Deliberations is on today's calendar. Before today's CPI, markets priced about a 40% chance of a BoC hike in December versus roughly 84% for the Fed.
Jobs: Canadian employment fell for a third straight month in October and the unemployment rate rose to 6.7%.
partner.takeaway: If someone asks you about markets today: a hotter CPI print pushed December Fed-hike odds higher, lifting short-term yields and the dollar. Tech, gold and crypto fell together, while small caps and defensives held up better.
partner.takeaway_consulting: Higher-for-longer rates raise the cost of capital for AI-heavy and leveraged businesses. A sensible strategy is to stress-test capex plans and financing at higher hurdle rates, and to avoid funding growth that only works at low rates.
partner.takeaway_accounting: For a large IPO such as Anthropic's, direct issuance costs are deducted from equity proceeds rather than expensed. Auditors would focus on revenue recognition, share-based compensation and valuation of any pre-IPO instruments. For Barrick's US listing, expect questions on carve-out financials and segment reporting.
